messages:
Maya: FYI a high-rep customer reported a sudden increase in 502/504 errors hitting our hosted inference endpoints around 11:20 PST. They're using streaming (chunked) responses and our SDK. They see a tight retry loop in their logs. I have their request sample and logs below and started INC-4321.
Maya: Customer: AcmeAnalytics (via support ticket). They can consistently repro by running a 30s-ish streaming generation that produces many tokens. Root error on client side: repeated 502s followed by a long 504.
Maya: Quick repro curl they used: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","stream":true,"prompt":"generate lots of text..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
``` 
Maya: Client logs show: ```
[2025-10-13T18:20:12Z] stream 12 error: HTTP/2 stream reset REFUSED_STREAM
[2025-10-13T18:20:12Z] request failed: upstream prematurely closed connection (502)
[2025-10-13T18:20:20Z] final error: read timeout (504)
``` 
Phil: Thanks. Looks similar to an earlier keepalive/backpressure issue but the twist here is streaming + HTTP/2 multiplexing on the SDK. Can you attach the proxy/gateway traces? I want to see whether the upstream container restarted or evicted connections.
Maya: Trace links: https://observability.internal/trace/INC-4321 and a short heap of gateway logs pasted in the ticket. Gateway shows repeated `client stream closed` followed by `upstream connection reset by peer` on the same per-instance worker.
Alex: I dug in — on the affected host we see bursts of >600 concurrent streaming connections from that customer (same token) which exceeds the per-worker stream limit (configured 500). The gateway tries to multiplex more streams, and the backend inference process begins to exhaust FDs and then closes idle/older streams. That generates REFUSED_STREAM/502 cascades.
Alex: Logs showing fd exhaustion: ```
[host-07] EMERG: cannot accept more connections: too many open files
[host-07] WARN: closing oldest stream id=1012 to recover
```
Jamie: Oof. That maps to a customer-side behavior: their SDK opened many parallel streaming sessions instead of reusing a single streaming connection. The SDK's default max concurrency is 50 but their integration spawned 600 parallel generator clients.
Maya: Customer confirms they run a fan-out across 600 workers to speed up throughput. They say previously it was fine; we must be resilient.
Phil: Short-term mitigation: increase gateway per-worker stream limit and raise ulimit on the hot hosts, plus a rate-limited token-level throttle for streaming. Medium-term: add per-token streaming-concurrency quota and better signals to reject early with 429 instead of letting backend hit FD limits.
Phil: I'm going to open a canary patch to bump stream limit from 500 -> 1024 on the fleet and raise net.core.somaxconn + ulimit for the few affected hosts.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/stream-limit-bump #789 -> canary (host-07)
deploy-bot: deploy status: canary succeeded on host-07 (5m)
Alex: Canary metrics look promising: rejected connections dropped, 502s disappeared on the canary host, latency normalized. However we still see a few 504s from clients that keep retrying aggressively.
Maya: For customer comms I suggested: "We've identified a concurrency-induced file-descriptor exhaustion on a subset of gateway hosts that caused stream resets and 502/504 cascades. We've deployed a canary fix and are rolling a temporary increase to connection limits while we implement token-level streaming quotas. Please avoid blasting >200 parallel streams per API key until we finalize fixes." They asked for ETA.
Phil: ETA: temporary ramp and throttles fully rolled in 2-3 hours, token quotas + client-side guidance doc within 24 hours. I'll also add SDK compatibility notes recommending connection reuse (single long-lived HTTP/2 connection or server-sent events) and exponential backoff with jitter.
Maya: Adding suggested SDK snippet to customer: ```js
// recommended: reuse one HTTP/2 session and do multiplexing
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
// pseudo: single streaming session + multiplexed requests rather than spawning N parallel
await client.stream({model: 'redwood-v1-large', prompt});
``` 
Jamie: Also flagged oncall to watch for host FD pressure; added alert threshold at 80% of ulimit.
Alex: Post-mortem notes (brief): root cause = unbounded client fan-out + insufficient per-host stream limits => FD exhaustion => upstream resets => SDK retry loops turning transient 502s into customer-visible outages. Remediation: 1) increase per-host stream limit temporarily, 2) implement token-based streaming concurrency quota, 3) publish SDK guidance and example code, 4) add early 429/Retry-After before hitting FD limits.
Maya: Customer updated: "Thanks, we'll throttle and test with the guidance. Appreciate the quick response." Closing loop: INC-4321 -> now tracking REM-550 (engineering work) for token quota.
Jamie: I'll keep the channel open for 2h to monitor but changing to follow-up status. If anyone sees new 502/504s spike, ping here. :thumbsup:
